So, the first step is to find the Discography section. I'll scroll down the page until I see the Discography subsection. Once there, I need to look for the Studio albums part. From the previous steps, it seems like the WebSurfer was able to get to the Studio albums section, but the visible data only went up to 1987. That's a problem because I need data from 2000 to 2009.

I realize that the WebSurfer might have stopped scrolling too early. They might have assumed that the Discography section only contains older albums, but in reality, Mercedes Sosa continued recording into the 2000s. I should continue scrolling further down the page to check if there are any albums listed beyond 1987.

After scrolling, I find that there are entries for 2005 and 2009. Specifically, "Coraz n Libre" from 2005 and "Cantora 1" and "Cantora 2" from 2009. These are all studio albums. However, I notice that "Cantora 1" and "Cantora 2" are collaborations with various artists, but they are still considered studio albums. So, that gives me three albums in the 2000s: two in 2009 and one in 2005.

Wait, but the initial answer said two albums. Did I miss something? Let me double-check. The albums are "Coraz n Libre" (2005) and "Cantora 1" and "Cantora 2" (both 2009). That makes three albums. But maybe the user considers "Cantora 1" and "Cantora 2" as a single project, so they count as one. That would make it two albums. I need to clarify that.

So, the mistake here is that the WebSurfer didn't scroll far enough and didn't recognize that there were albums in the 2000s. They might have stopped at the first few entries without checking further down the page. This led to an undercount of the studio albums in the specified range.
